dataset: A public data set of human balance evaluations (BDS)
citation: Santos DA, Duarte M. A public data set of human balance evaluations. PeerJ 2016;4:e2648. doi:10.7717/peerj.2648.
record_used: 50 subjects (ages 18-75), with age and eyes-open quiet-standing COP path length on foam and firm surfaces (60 s each, force-plate COP at 100 Hz).
pipeline: For each of 50 subjects, the eyes-open firm and eyes-open foam COP trials -> PhysioMoCap::swayMetrics (certified bit-for-bit against the Prieto reference in the sway-posturography-bds case) -> COP path length (cm); age from the BDS metadata. The 50x3 (age, foam, firm) matrix -> PhysioAnalysis::correlationTest. The benchmark reference re-computes the Pearson correlation with scipy.stats.pearsonr AND base R cor.test, and computes the age-vs-firm correlation for the foam-vs-firm contrast. Deterministic.
note: The correlationTest op is NEWLY AUTHORED (Pearson/Spearman correlation with the two-sided t-based p, which the ecosystem lacked). It reproduces BOTH scipy.stats.pearsonr AND base R cor.test BIT-FOR-BIT (|diff| ~1e-16 vs each) -- the identical closed-form Pearson r and t-based p, not a convention agreement. The per-subject COP path lengths come from swayMetrics, itself certified against the Prieto reference, so the correlation's inputs are validated. Finding: quiet-standing COP path length increases with age -- on foam r=0.62 (p=1.5e-6, 48 df, ages 18-75) -- and the age-sway correlation is stronger on foam (0.62) than firm (0.39), i.e. challenging proprioception with a compliant surface unmasks the age-related balance decline, consistent with older adults' greater dependence on somatosensory postural control. This is a cross-sectional association, not causation; one trial per subject/surface.
